liability.description: Covers damages you cause to others in an accident
what_it_covers: Legal defense costs if you're sued
what_it_doesnt_cover: Your own injuries or vehicle damage

collision.description: Covers damage to your vehicle from collisions
what_it_covers: Damage from hitting objects (trees, poles, etc.)

comprehensive.description: Covers damage to your vehicle from non-collision events

uninsured_motorist.description: Protects you when hit by uninsured/underinsured drivers

dwelling.description: Covers the structure of your home

personal_property.description: Covers your belongings inside and outside the home

deductible.definition: Amount you pay out-of-pocket before insurance coverage begins
deductible.how_it_works: Higher deductible = Lower premium. You choose this amount when buying coverage.
deductible.example: With $500 deductible and $3000 claim, you pay $500, insurance pays $2500

premium.definition: The amount you pay for insurance coverage
premium.how_it_works: Based on risk factors, coverage amounts, and deductible choices

policy_period.definition: Time period your insurance coverage is active
policy_period.renewal_process: Automatic renewal unless cancelled by you or insurer

exclusions.definition: Specific situations or damages not covered by your policy

auto_scenarios.scenario: I hit a deer while driving
auto_scenarios.explanation: Animal collisions are covered under comprehensive coverage, not collision

auto_scenarios.scenario: Someone rear-ends me and they don't have insurance
auto_scenarios.explanation: Your uninsured motorist coverage pays for your injuries and potentially vehicle damage
Your liability coverage pays for the other person's damages and injuries
Theft is covered under comprehensive coverage
Weather-related damage is covered under comprehensive coverage

home_scenarios.scenario: A tree falls on my house during a storm
home_scenarios.explanation: Storm damage to your home structure is covered under dwelling coverage

home_scenarios.scenario: Someone is injured on my property
home_scenarios.explanation: Personal liability coverage pays for injuries to others on your property

home_scenarios.scenario: My laptop is stolen from my car
home_scenarios.explanation: Personal belongings are covered even when away from home
Sudden water damage is typically covered, but gradual leaks may not be

auto_factors.explanation: Insurance companies use 3-5 year history to assess risk

auto_factors.impact: Expensive or high-performance cars cost more to insure
auto_factors.explanation: Based on repair costs, theft rates, and safety ratings

auto_factors.impact: Urban areas typically have higher rates
auto_factors.explanation: Higher accident rates and theft in densely populated areas
More coverage = higher potential payouts = higher premium
You take on more financial responsibility

home_factors.impact: More expensive homes cost more to insure
home_factors.explanation: Higher replacement costs require higher coverage limits

home_factors.impact: Areas prone to natural disasters cost more
home_factors.explanation: Flood zones, earthquake areas, hurricane regions have higher rates

home_factors.impact: Older homes may cost more due to higher risk
home_factors.explanation: Older electrical, plumbing, and roofing increase claim likelihood

home_factors.impact: Security systems and smoke detectors reduce premium
home_factors.explanation: Risk reduction measures lower claim probability
